body.purpose: Adjustable single-line type shared by the root menu, search, submenus, and shortcut context menus.

settings.purpose: Native dialog controls and explanatory labels.

components.name: Tray Menu
components.description: Rounded Windows 11-inspired root or nested menu surface.
components.html:
Application shortcut

components.css: .ds-tray-menu { width: 280px; padding: 6px 4px; background: #F9F9F9; color: #1F1F1F; border: 1px solid #D6D6D6; border-radius: 8px; font: 400 10pt 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.18); } .ds-menu-row { min-height: 36px; margin: 0 4px; padding: 0 12px; display: flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 4px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-menu-row:hover, .ds-menu-row:focus-visible { background: #E8E8E8; outline: none; } .ds-menu-row:active { background: #E0E0E0; } .ds-separator { height: 1px; margin: 4px 12px; background: #D6D6D6; }

components.name: Menu Row
components.description: Single-line shortcut or utility action with tonal pointer states.
components.css: .ds-row { width: 272px; min-height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #F9F9F9; color: #1F1F1F; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; font: 400 10pt 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; text-align: left; } .ds-row:hover, .ds-row:focus-visible { background: #E8E8E8; outline: none; } .ds-row:active { background: #E0E0E0; } .ds-row:disabled { color: #969696; } .ds-row-label { white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-row-icon { width: 16px; height: 16px; flex: 0 0 16px; }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: Inset shortcut filter with search and conditional clear glyphs.
components.css: .ds-search { width: 264px; height: 38px; padding: 0 12px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; background: #F3F3F3; color: #616161; border: 1px solid #D6D6D6; border-radius: 8px; font: 400 10pt 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-search:hover { border-color: #ACACAC; } .ds-search:focus-within { border: 2px solid #0067C0; padding: 0 11px; } .ds-search-icon { width: 16px; height: 16px; flex: 0 0 16px; } .ds-search-input { min-width: 0; flex: 1; background: transparent; color: #1F1F1F; border: 0; outline: 0; font: inherit; } .ds-search-clear { width: 20px; text-align: center; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; }

components.name: Nested Menu Row
components.description: Category or profile entry that exposes the same styled descendant surface.
components.css: .ds-nested-row { width: 272px; min-height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; background: #F9F9F9; color: #1F1F1F; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; font: 400 10pt 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; text-align: left; } .ds-nested-row svg { width: 12px; height: 12px; color: #616161; } .ds-nested-row:hover, .ds-nested-row:focus-visible { background: #E8E8E8; outline: none; } .ds-nested-row:active { background: #E0E0E0; }

components.name: Settings Group
components.description: Native group-box organization used throughout the fixed Settings dialog.
components.html: <fieldset class="ds-settings-group"><legend>Menu Appearance</legend><label>Item height: <input type="number" min="32" max="72" step="2" value="36"/> px</label><label>Text size: <input type="number" min="9" max="18" step="0.5" value="10"/> pt</label></fieldset>
components.css: .ds-settings-group { width: 440px; padding: 12px; display: grid; gap: 12px; background: #F9F9F9; color: #1F1F1F; border: 1px solid #D6D6D6; font: 400 9.5pt 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-settings-group legend { padding: 0 4px; } .ds-settings-group label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-settings-group input { width: 64px; min-height: 23px; font: inherit; } .ds-settings-group input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0067C0; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Settings Button
components.description: Native-sized dialog action used for OK, Cancel, Choose, Remove, and management actions.
components.css: .ds-settings-button { min-width: 80px; height: 28px; padding: 0 12px; background: #F3F3F3; color: #1F1F1F; border: 1px solid #D6D6D6; border-radius: 3px; font: 400 9.5pt 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-settings-button:hover { background: #E8E8E8; } .ds-settings-button:active { background: #E0E0E0; } .ds-settings-button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0067C0; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-settings-button:disabled { color: #969696; }

narrative.overview:
TaskFolder is a compact Windows utility, not a branded dashboard. Its visual system replaces legacy Win32 menu chrome with a restrained Windows 11-inspired surface while preserving the speed, density, hierarchy, and interaction model users expect from a tray launcher. The root tray menu, category and profile submenus, and shortcut context menus must feel like one continuous native system.

The design is quiet and functional: warm-neutral surfaces, crisp dark text, soft corners, one-pixel structure, and a single blue focus signal. Shortcut icons and the optional user-selected logo carry the visual identity; decoration must never compete with scanability or one-click launching.

The tokens and component behavior below were extracted from the WinForms/GDI implementation. Static review and the Release build passed with a SHIP disposition; actual Windows GUI appearance at 100–200% display scaling remains to be verified on representative monitors.
keyCharacteristics: One renderer across root, nested, and right-click menus.
Adjustable menu type and row height stored as device-local logical values.
Solid tonal states, precise dividers, and OS-provided menu shadow.
Native settings controls rather than a custom web-like control kit.

rules.name: The Blue Means Focus Rule
rules.body: Use focus-blue only for a live focus affordance unless a future implemented control establishes another interaction role.

rules.name: The Solid-State Rule
rules.body: Hover and pressed feedback use solid tonal fills; do not reintroduce glossy Win32 gradients.

rules.name: The One Type Voice Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce headings or novelty faces into tray-menu rows; logo imagery is the optional branding moment.

rules.name: The Logical Size Rule
rules.body: Persist point size as an unscaled preference, then let WinForms and the current monitor DPI produce the physical result.

rules.name: The Whole Tree Rule
rules.body: Any new submenu or shortcut context action must be created through the shared Windows 11 menu classes so it inherits the same renderer and DPI behavior.

rules.name: The Scale Once Rule
rules.body: Treat stored row height, field size, radius, padding, and offsets as 96-DPI logical values; scale them once against the owning control's DeviceDpi.

rules.name: The Native Shadow Rule
rules.body: Let Windows own context-menu shadow rendering; do not approximate it with a second custom shadow layer.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: Outer surfaces and fields use the larger radius; transient row highlights use the smaller radius and remain inset from the edge.

dos: Do use the shared renderer, context-menu class, and font factory for every tray, nested, and shortcut context surface.
Do preserve a single-line, vertically centered, ellipsized label in every adjustable-height menu row.
Do scale logical menu geometry from the owning control's current DPI and keep persisted preferences unscaled.
Do use native WinForms controls and Windows visual styles for Settings unless implementation establishes a complete replacement system.
Do preserve visible default, hover/selected, pressed, disabled, separator, checked, and focused-search states.
donts: Don't mix a legacy-rendered submenu or context menu into the Windows 11 menu tree.
Don't use blue as decoration, a row hover fill, or a general brand wash; it currently means focused text entry.
Don't add gradients, extra shadows, translucency, animation, or ornamental typography that is absent from the implementation.
Don't wrap menu labels or allow text size to change the configured minimum row rhythm.
Don't claim 100–200% DPI behavior is visually verified until the real GUI has been exercised on representative Windows displays.
